title: Restore lighting automatically at startup and after reconnect
summary: Make everyday startup and USB recovery dependable without repeated manual setup.
criteria: Offer opt-in launch at login and automatic controller connection on Windows and macOS.
Restore the last power state, profile, and non-capture mode after restart or reconnect.
Resume capture only where OS permission and user intent allow; explain when a new action is required.
Verify unplug/replug, busy-device recovery, and prevention of duplicate app instances on hardware.

title: Follow display sleep, computer lock, and wake state
summary: Avoid leaving lights on when the display is asleep, while restoring the intended state on return.
criteria: Distinguish display-only sleep, session lock, and computer suspend on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Allow independent off-on-sleep and off-on-lock preferences.
Restore the prior lighting state on wake without enabling lights that were already off.
Prevent write races during suspend and resume; test each transition on physical hardware.

title: Improve screen sync with black-bar detection and color calibration
summary: Make screen lighting follow the visible picture accurately and smoothly.
criteria: Detect letterbox/pillarbox regions and optionally exclude them from sampling.
Provide RGB balance, saturation, gamma, and response-speed adjustments with reset defaults.
Handle scene changes without excessive lag or brightness spikes.
Document SDR/HDR limitations and validate representative video content on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

title: Add a guided LED-by-LED calibration wizard
summary: Identify the strip's first LED, direction, count, and physical placement using visible test patterns.
criteria: Step through individual LEDs with clear next/previous and stop controls.
Identify starting corner, travel direction, and usable LED count.
Save a calibrated mapping and preview it before applying.
Restore the prior lighting state on completion or cancellation.

title: Save profiles and switch them with global shortcuts
summary: Create reusable Work, Movies, Gaming, and custom lighting profiles.
criteria: Create, rename, duplicate, delete, and reorder named profiles.
Include mode, colors, brightness, and relevant capture/effect settings.
Switch profiles from the tray and configurable global keyboard shortcuts.
Detect shortcut conflicts and require fresh capture consent when necessary.

title: Add bass, frequency-band, and beat-reactive music effects
summary: Expand music mode beyond a single frequency-to-brightness mapping.
criteria: Offer bass pulse, spectrum bands, and beat-reactive effect presets.
Expose input gain, sensitivity, smoothing, and silence behavior.
Support computer audio and microphone sources with a visible signal meter.
Validate actual audio response, permission failures, and device changes on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

title: Add connection diagnostics and redacted log export
summary: Make intermittent USB and capture failures diagnosable.
criteria: Show connection state, write failures, dropped frames, actual FPS, and capture status.
Keep a bounded local diagnostic log with clear retention controls.
Preview and redact private paths, serial numbers, and captured content before export.
Provide actionable recovery guidance and a copyable troubleshooting summary.

title: Support multiple monitors and independent LED controllers
summary: Assign separate strips to displays and control them together or independently.
criteria: Identify each supported lighting interface without opening keyboard interfaces.
Map each controller to a display and independent calibration/profile.
Support grouped power/brightness while preserving per-device settings.
Recover from monitor rearrangement and one device disconnecting without stopping others.
scopeNote: Display selection already exists. This issue adds simultaneous independent controllers and per-controller routing.

title: Switch profiles automatically for selected applications
summary: Apply a game, video, or work profile when an application becomes active.
criteria: Create rules for explicitly selected apps and define precedence.
Restore the previous scene when the matching app exits or loses focus.
Provide manual override and a clear explanation of the active rule.
Avoid uploading application-usage information; handle platform permission requirements.

title: Schedule lighting scenes and gradual transitions
summary: Schedule evening warmth, morning fades, and automatic shutoff.
criteria: Create recurring local-time schedules with selected days and profiles.
Support fade-in, fade-out, and immediate transitions.
Handle daylight-saving changes, missed events, sleep, and timezone changes predictably.
Provide pause/override controls and show the next scheduled action.

title: Build a custom lighting effects editor
summary: Author gradients, waves, breathing patterns, and custom color sequences.
criteria: Edit colors, keyframes, duration, repetition, speed, and direction with a live preview.
Create and combine gradient, wave, and breathing building blocks.
Save reusable effects with a versioned format.
Cancel edits without replacing the active scene; bound CPU and USB work.
scopeNote: Built-in effects already have speed and direction controls. This issue adds custom effect authoring.

title: Control independent strip zones
summary: Give the monitor's left, top, right, and optional bottom edges separate lighting behavior.
criteria: Create named zones from calibrated LED ranges.
Assign static colors or compatible effects per zone.
Define overlap handling and global power/brightness precedence.
Preview and save zone layouts with profiles.

title: Capture a selected window or screen region
summary: Follow a video window or selected region rather than the entire display.
criteria: Offer full-display, application-window, and rectangular-region sources.
Preview the selected region and map its edges to the strip.
Handle movement, resizing, minimization, source closure, and display scaling.
Stop cleanly when capture is revoked and document protected-content limitations.
scopeNote: Full-display capture already exists. Window and rectangle capture remain unimplemented.

title: Add brightness and flash comfort controls
summary: Let users limit abrupt changes and maintain comfortable background lighting.
criteria: Provide configurable maximum brightness and brightness-change rate limits.
Offer optional flash softening and a minimum ambient glow.
Apply limits consistently to screen, audio, and custom effects.
Keep an immediate off control and explain that comfort settings are not a medical safety guarantee.

title: Show temporary notification accents
summary: Briefly signal selected events or timers without losing the active scene.
criteria: Allow explicit event sources and configurable accent colors/durations.
Restore the previous scene and power state after each accent.
Respect quiet hours, comfort limits, and user-disabled lighting.
Queue or coalesce simultaneous events and avoid reading notification content unnecessarily.

title: Expose a local automation API and command-line controls
summary: Control lighting from scripts, Stream Deck, and home-automation integrations.
criteria: Define versioned commands for status, power, brightness, scenes, and profiles.
Bind locally by default and authenticate requests.
Document examples for shell scripts and Stream Deck; outline home-automation adapters.
Validate and rate-limit commands without bypassing comfort limits or capture permission.

title: Add a paired phone remote on the local network
summary: Adjust lighting from a phone without a cloud account.
criteria: Serve a responsive remote for power, brightness, colors, and saved profiles.
Require explicit opt-in LAN access and a pairing flow with revocation.
Protect the remote against unauthorized requests and avoid exposing capture data.
Show connected clients and handle host sleep or disconnection gracefully.

title: Export and import portable profiles across platforms
summary: Move lighting settings between Windows, macOS, and Linux or share a scene.
criteria: Export selected profiles and effects to a versioned file format.
Validate imports and preview conflicts before replacing any settings.
Separate portable preferences from machine-specific device/display bindings.
Exclude secrets and private paths; provide backup and migration behavior.

title: Add a neutral-white bias-lighting mode
summary: Provide an adjustable neutral-white mode for films and color-sensitive work.
criteria: Offer a neutral-white target and brightness controls with per-channel calibration.
Save calibrated presets separately from decorative effects.
Explain the limits of RGB strips and avoid claiming color accuracy without measurement.
Support measured calibration inputs where practical and retain ordinary power controls.
scopeNote: Fixed colors and screen RGB balance already exist. This issue adds a dedicated calibrated bias-lighting workflow; RGB neutrality requires measurement.

title: Blend screen colors with music-reactive brightness
summary: Combine screen ambience and audio response in a single scene.
criteria: Sample screen colors while modulating brightness or selected zones from audio.
Expose blend strength, sensitivity, and smoothing.
Fall back predictably when one capture source stops or becomes silent.
Respect comfort limits and avoid competing USB writers.

title: Extract lighting palettes from images and wallpaper
summary: Create a lighting theme from a photo, wallpaper, or supplied album-cover image.
criteria: Import an image locally and suggest a compact palette.
Allow editing, reordering, and saving palette colors.
Apply the palette to static zones or compatible effects.
Offer wallpaper-derived palettes where supported without uploading the source image.

title: Record and replay lighting sequences
summary: Replay a short captured lighting sequence without ongoing screen capture.
criteria: Record bounded RGB frame sequences with duration and storage limits.
Replay, loop, trim, and adjust speed from an offline file.
Store lighting data only, not source screenshots or audio.
Handle different LED layouts through an explicit remapping step.

title: Adapt brightness to an ambient-light sensor
summary: Adjust lighting to room conditions when a supported sensor is available.
criteria: Discover supported OS or external sensor sources and show availability.
Map sensor values to user-defined minimum/maximum brightness.
Smooth changes and preserve manual override.
Fall back to a fixed level if the sensor becomes unavailable.

title: Add game telemetry integrations
summary: Reflect health, cooldowns, and team colors through games' supported telemetry.
criteria: Start with a documented, explicitly supported game telemetry interface.
Map selected events to lighting zones or temporary effects.
Require opt-in and avoid process injection or anti-cheat interference.
Restore the ordinary profile when the game or telemetry connection ends.

title: Add focus and break timers with lighting cues
summary: Use subtle lighting changes to mark work sessions and breaks.
criteria: Configure work/break durations and optional repeated cycles.
Show remaining time and provide start, pause, skip, and cancel controls.
Use configurable cues and restore the previous scene afterward.
Respect quiet hours, off state, and comfort settings.

title: Coordinate device handoff between Windows and Mac
summary: Make switching a strip between computers predictable while respecting physical USB ownership.
criteria: Release the device cleanly before a USB switch or unplug.
Restore a compatible profile when the controller appears on the other host.
Explain that physical USB switching is required unless a separate network bridge is configured.
Prevent competing ownership and provide a manual recovery path.

title: Define a plugin system for effects and integrations
summary: Extend effects and integrations without modifying the core app.
criteria: Specify a versioned plugin manifest and lifecycle API.
Separate effect processing from integrations with explicit capabilities.
Isolate failures, limit resource usage, and require opt-in for sensitive access.
Provide a sample plugin and install/disable/remove controls without arbitrary renderer privileges.

title: Make the monitor and LED preview interactive
summary: Edit physical placement and colors by interacting directly with the preview.
criteria: Select individual LEDs, ranges, or monitor edges with visible selection state.
Edit placement and supported color/zone properties from the selection.
Support keyboard selection and undo/cancel behavior.
Clearly distinguish simulated preview from connected hardware output.
scopeNote: The passive monitor preview and guided calibration already exist. This issue adds direct LED/edge selection and editing.

title: Add a color wheel, temperature control, and saved palettes
summary: Make color selection richer and reusable.
criteria: Provide a color wheel with RGB/hex input and accessible keyboard alternatives.
Add a temperature slider with clear RGB approximation semantics.
Keep recent colors and named saved palettes.
Show live preview while preserving reset/cancel behavior.
scopeNote: Native color input, fixed effect palettes and recent tray colors already exist. The wheel, temperature control and named editable palettes remain.

title: Create a visual scene-card library
summary: Offer browsable preview cards for built-in and saved scenes.
criteria: Include Warm Desk, Cinema, Neon, and Ocean starter scenes.
Show a representative preview and key settings on each card.
Support favorites, search/filter, duplication, and applying a scene.
Honor reduced-motion preferences and make active/simulated states clear.

title: Build focused mode-specific control panels
summary: Show controls relevant to the selected lighting mode without clutter.
criteria: Use dedicated Screen Sync, Music, Solid, and Effects panels.
Include a live audio signal/spectrum visualizer in Music.
Expose speed/direction in Effects and capture source/calibration in Screen Sync.
Preserve each mode's settings and explain disabled controls or missing permissions.

title: Add a compact floating lighting controller
summary: Offer quick controls without keeping the full studio window open.
criteria: Provide power, brightness, and favorite-scene controls in a small window.
Offer optional always-on-top behavior and remember position within visible screen bounds.
Keep state synchronized with the main window and tray.
Support keyboard use, scaling, and a clear return-to-studio action.

title: Add a rich tray and macOS menu-bar control panel
summary: Adjust lighting directly from the system tray or menu bar.
criteria: Expose power, brightness, recent colors, and favorite profiles.
Show connection/capture status with a direct recovery action.
Synchronize changes with the studio and floating controller.
Respect native platform placement, keyboard behavior, and light/dark appearance.

title: Add drag-and-drop monitor and strip layout setup
summary: Arrange monitors and draw the strip's physical route visually.
criteria: Display monitor arrangement and allow explicit controller-to-monitor mapping.
Draw or adjust LED paths, corners, offsets, and edge coverage.
Provide keyboard/form alternatives to dragging.
Preview mappings and validate them before applying to hardware.
scopeNote: Single-strip calibration already exists. This issue adds visual routing and arrangement for multiple monitors/controllers.

title: Show actionable connection and capture states
summary: Make Connected, Reconnecting, Capture paused, and Permission needed states understandable.
criteria: Define a consistent state model across the studio, tray, and compact controller.
Present a relevant action beside each recoverable state.
Distinguish USB connection from active lighting and active capture.
Announce changes accessibly without repetitive alerts or color-only indicators.

title: Add themes, accent colors, and layout density options
summary: Personalize appearance while preserving readability.
criteria: Support light, dark, and follow-system themes.
Offer accent colors and compact/spacious layouts.
Persist preferences and apply them across all app surfaces.
Maintain sufficient contrast and test scaling and long labels.
scopeNote: A separate compact controller already exists. Theme, accent and studio density preferences remain unimplemented.

title: Validate accessibility across studio, Quick controls and tray
summary: Audit the implemented controls with keyboard and assistive technology; fix or link any discovered defects before closing.
criteria: Provide complete keyboard navigation, visible focus, and semantic control names/states.
Verify readable contrast, larger interaction targets, and display scaling.
Respect reduced-motion preferences for UI animations and previews.
Test with Windows and macOS screen readers and provide alternatives to drag-only controls.
Verify connection/capture announcements without repeated alerts or color-only status (#35).
Check scene search, favorites, dialogs, shortcuts and return-to-studio in the main and compact windows.

title: Validate macOS 0.6 releases on Intel and Apple Silicon
summary: Validate the existing DMG builds on physical Macs, recording architecture, OS version and controller; track accessibility separately in #37.
criteria: Produce installable Intel and Apple Silicon builds in macOS CI.
Verify USB control, screen capture, computer audio/microphone, and permission flows on a Mac.
Validate tray behavior, reconnect, and sleep/wake with physical hardware.
Document signing/notarization status, installation steps, and remaining platform limitations.
Run the full lifecycle and studio checklists, including calibration, profiles, diagnostics, mode memory and Quick controls.
Record results and link reproducible defects; do not count CI builds as hardware validation.

title: Validate Windows and Linux 0.6 on physical hardware
summary: Validate the implemented 0.6 features on Windows and Linux desktops. Physical testing is deferred; no new hardware results are claimed.
criteria: Record app build, OS/desktop/session, controller, monitor arrangement and audio route for each run.

Run every applicable lifecycle-testing.md scenario: install/upgrade, login restore, Stop persistence, USB busy/replug, nested lock/sleep/wake, display sleep, audio/display changes, permissions, single instance and login entry.
Run studio-testing.md: profiles/shortcuts, tray, calibration apply/cancel/Stop, screen color and SDR/HDR limitations, music input/routing, blend fallback and comfort controls.
Check diagnostic report preview/copy/export and history controls, mode memory and effect direction.
Check Quick controls across monitor/DPI changes, pinning, position restoration, studio/tray synchronization, and scene application.
Record pass/fail/not applicable with reasons for each OS; link defects and retest fixes before closing. Accessibility is tracked in #37; macOS in #38.
